This article first appeared in the German libertarian magazine "eigentümlich frei", of which Hoppe is a board member.

The so-called "right-wing populism" was a natural result and political counter-movement to the impertinences of the rulers over years and decades. This counter-movement led to an increasing politicization and polarization of our society, and it was unavoidable. So far, everything was predictable. Soon enough the new political apprentices will disenchant their own followers, people will lose their trust into the state and politics, and then, after many years, maybe decades, if they have dotted the i's and crossed the t's, the Hour of Libertarians could dawn and true solutions to ending the political vicious circle of interventionism could be found. They are already needed!

Libertarians? Well, for the last 20 years their ideas have quietly become increasingly popular. There were numerous magnets, often independently from each other: Ron Paul, Oliver Janich, Bitcoin, Goldbucks. And "Eigentümlich Frei" published more and more copies each month. The formerly tiny crowd has grown much larger. And yet, many especially young Libertarians view the Identitarian Movement with a mix of envy and hope, who manage to be the town's talk while hardly anyone speaks of Libertarianism.

A few thoughts about that, which I want to start with some navel-gazing: Who represents "the Libertarians" and especially "the Libertarian youth" in Germany? Are there structural similarities or differences to the Identitarians?

There are a few diligent bloggers and vloggers in both camps. Magazines, book publishers, societies and institutes as well as loose groups are as well found on both sides. But a "Libertarian Movement" analogous to the "Identitarian Movement" is nowhere to be found - and so agitprop actions from the roof of the Reichstag won't happen.

What do Libertarians and Identitarians want? Libertarians fight for "the only human right, the right to be left alone" (Roland Baader). Which is very accurate at its core and yet somewhat misleading, as very few Libertarians are egomaniacs who only care to achieve an advantage to themselves. Rather, Libertarians are primarily idealists and driven by a strong sense of justice (as are Identitarians). It's less about being left alone yourself, but rather about ensuring that B will also be left alone by C without having the fruits of his labour and his trade stolen. Eventually the goal is ensuring freedom through property by the insight that freedom can only be guaranteed through private property.

As everyone has different plans for their property, Libertarians don't fight for concrete contents, but for the rules of the game: Contract instead of dictate, private property instead of collective property, market instead of state to as the tools of conflict resolution. Bluntly said, libertarian ideas aren't political, but antipolitical. Although this important insight is misleading too. Just as Atheism can be identified as a religious outlook, because it revolves around answers to religious questions, fights the Libertarian for political questions as he denies the suggorate god of the state.

But "differently". This will become more clear as I approach concrete issues. For example, Libertarians criticize mass immigration just as Identitarians do. Libertarians point at the welfare incentives, which cause to mass immigration in the first place, as well as at the war-monging foreign policy of the Western powers in the home region of the immigrants, which also caused the wave. Libertarians don't trust into the problem-solving abilities of the notorically ailing and corrupt forced monopolists and neither call for them. Rather, they would scale back or completely shut down the state in its aggressive interventionism and welfare magnetism, and thus break up the wave.

Identitarians don't think anti-politically, but politically. They still believe in the almighty god of the state, despite being a "movement" and not a party. They call for it to close the borders. The two leading identitarians Martin Sellner and Patrick Lenart announced in a video discussion, how much the two incorrigible statists Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel and Alain de Benoist shaped their line of thinking. It is therefore hardly surprising that they believe that "Criticism of Mass Immigration" must simultanously be "Criticism of Capitalism", as allegedly businesses caused the current immigration wave to force wage dumping. Ouch.

Do those two really believe that the famous 23 refugees working in DAX companies among the more than one million unemployable young men are "profitable"? It would be nice if most of the immigrants had arrived to become productive. But is it that way? Why shouldn't of all groups businesses realize that they will be the ones who will have to pay for skyrocketing costs of care, supply and accomodation for the cultural strangers? Why, for example, should a middle class entrepreneur voluntarily destroy his home country and the future of his children? And for which ends?

Nope, obviously the mass immigration of these days is not caused by the market or capitalism, but typical fruit of the political vicious circle of state interventionism. And if for example George Soros aids pulling the lever, then he is led by sinister ideological goals, but precisely not by entrepreneurial profits. And as needs to be noted, the globally acting mega-corporations, which are personified by Soros, are part of the Big Business/Big Government conglomerate and are not participating in actual capitalism, as it was the state that enabled them in the first place. But this is a different story for another day.

So why are Libertarians on the defense, despite continual growth and superior problem-solving abilities? For one, because society is highly politicized and highly polarized and the disenchantment of "right-wing populism" as yet another crony of statist interventionism only has just started (although it is happening faster than expected). Second, the defensive libertarian position could be caused by a group about which we haven't spoken yet, but which seemingly represents libertarian ideas at German universities among other places - let's call them "Liberalalas". Liberalalas read (more or less) the same books as Libertarians (maybe not Rothbard and Hoppe, but certainly Hayek and occasionally Mises). They too talk all the time about freedom, and they too have grown in recent years.

But libertarian criticism is at its core always criticism of rulership, is always a radical challenge to the statist establishment - and in this point Liberalalas show their true face, as they don't warn about the rampant madness of the government, but about those who warn about it. And thus Liberalalas are fierce fighters "against the right", side by side with the net state profiteers.

And thus it comes that Liberalalas, for example, champion establishment's first choice Emmanuel Macron as saviour of France. Unlike Libertarians, Liberalalas are not the least bit anti-political, but are cheering for politics. In videos of their congresses, visitors lured by free food and drink swoon over how much they "love political events", to "do build a network of good contacts" for their latter jobs in Berlin, Bruxelles or Washington. Liberalalaism as a career boost.

Liberalalas are especially "very cosmopolitan" - every sense of belonging is unknown to them. Their student organizations, their office titles within them and even their internal magazine ("Peace Lover Liberty", in German roughly "Peace Joy Pancake") receive embarassing English names. German is gauche.

A swift excursion on that: The author and lecturer Michael Seemann has in October 2016 published a much observed article. Originally written for the neo-leftost "Jungle World", which rejected it, it was finally published in "Tagesspiegel" under the title "The Global Class". Seemann wrote a psychogram of the same aloof caste that was surprised by Trump's victory and considered it to be the end of the world. And Seeman, which is the gag about it, deems himself one of them. Finally, he also gives a good description of Liberalalas.

There is "today a globalized class of information workers, to which most of us belong and which is more homogenous and powerful than is commonly assumed. They are well-educated by young people, which are culturally increasingly global-leaning, who read "New York Times" instead of watching German public broadcasting, who have many foreign friends and friends abroad, who travel a lot, but not necessarily on vacation. It is a class that leaves virtually exclusively in great cities, that speaks English as fluently as its native tongue, for who Europe isn't an abstraction, but reality as they move from Madrid to Stockholm for their next job." This "new globalized class is found in media, in start-ups and NGOs, in political parties, and because it controls the flow of information, it sets the pace culturally and politically. This class has been derived from the bourgeoisie, but has empancipated from it."

(continued in comments)
André F. Lichtschlag - Liberalala, Libertarian, Identitarian: A Culture and Class Analysis

(cont.)

These "progressive increasingly globally oriented", as Seemann continues, "have left everyone else simply behind. The global class has produced very wealthy individuals, especially in Silicon Valley, but interestingly they use their wealth to transform it into discoursive capital: Into other start-ups, or into ambitioned save-the-world programs. Because secretly they know the true source of their power: The control of discourse and morals." And this exactly what "the others notice, the culturally backwards. They notice that our world has grown too small, that we feel morally superior and that we strive for something greater. Especially they notice that we are successful at that, that we define the standards which will be increasingly used on themselves. Politically correct standards. And the standards that are discarded and thrown out by this process have originally come from the bourgeoisie, at a time when they still had their say. It's cultural gentrification."

Well observed - this new cultural class warfare divides society. The cleave goes across a diverse selection of groups, it divides different kinds of Christianity. And it divides Liberalalas from Libertarians, who now find themselves on different sides of the fission.

And what is also important for our observation: In this cleave, in this new class war and Kulturkampf Libertarians and Identitarians are standing on the same side - against the seemingly related Liberalalas with their politically correct boilerplate phrases and their rulership legitimation. This relatedness is it, that makes Identitarians so attractive to young Libertarians, often unconsciously so.

To both groups, the door-to-door salesmen of the Liberalalas with their hyper-woke globalist perspective must appear like caricatures at a time when the own home country is possibly breaking apart.

And in this "no future" feeling is the final important point to understanding the momentum of the new right and the Identitarians. Similarly to the Green movement in the 1980s, they profit off a sense of alarmism that penetrates far beyond its core group. As the end of the world used to be signalled by forest dieback and ozone depletion, it is now marked by mass immigration and replacement migration. From the point of view of the doom sayers, the world is once again on razor's edge.

Such an enragement, such a deeply felt drive, releases forces. A catalyst that the Libertarians currently seem to lack, as just because of increasing taxation, a few more surveillance measures, more dirigism and redistribution, no one sacrifices their civil life and suddenly risks "it all".

Also: That which is forbidden, is especially appealing to us! Another aspect for the attractiveness of the Identitarians, who are threatened by domestic intelligence and so seemingly rise to hero status. By the way: What a pathetic course of the AfD, that their party youth dudes immediately seek "distance" to the Identitarians, instead of standing in front of them as the state applied the thumb screws. Characterless Liberalalas seem to exist in every flavour.

Libertarians should be aware that when they massively question the "alternativeless directions" of our government, that, when they truly have their time in the limelight one day, it will only be a matter of time until the bat of domestic intelligence is swung against them. It is really rather weird, that this bat is swung against the Identitarians who actually just want to protect our constitutional order against the lawless and unconstitutional crimes of the ruling crimelords. Who could be a greater enemy of the constitution than a true friend of liberty, who for example questions the duty to redistribute wealth and agitates against the welfare clause of our constitution?

That doesn't mean that every Libertarian has now to become a martyr, not all. But who wants to understand why the Identitarians are currently so appealing must realize that they "go for where it hurts". These young people risk very much for their ideals, sacrifice their burgeois career, stand up against the ruling class and their a-fascist street thugs. That is what young people do, yes: Young men. And only them.

Others in the background support them in this endeavour - last but not least especially financially, without risking anything personally. For this purpose the new right has specially funded "Initiative 1%", a master piece copied from the left ("Rote Hilfe"/Red Aid). A tactic that could also be copied by Libertarians, when they not only wish to play pretend, if they want to question the powers that be without seeking power for themselves, but only to destroy the structures of the enforced monopolies.

We'd need both: Young bravos and supporters in the background. Why should it be impossible to organize that? Shouldn't youths of all groups dare something, those who want more than to march under a fake freedom flag to the state-sponsored pork barrels like the Liberalalas? If we have a lot of fun while also going medieval for liberty?

Some Libertarians may even be active with the Identitarians. Why not, maybe we can dispel some statist illusions that way. On the same side of the class divide we stand - and this deep chasm not only divides Libertarians from Liberalalas, but also the New Right and Identitarians from fake rightist party youth dudes and career seekers within the AfD. Insofar there are some great similarities between Libertarians and Identitarians, at least as long as they haven't achieved into a position of power.

Let's not lie to ourselves: The current strength of Identitarians and New Right took years of preparing work. Work that was especially in Schnellroda. "Eigentümlich Frei" has made a start with its competition for young first-time authors. This needs to be expanded and enhanced. We are ready for it. Who's able to become the libertarian Martin Sellner, who himself is something like the Rudi Dutschke of our days, time will tell. We can afford to be optimistic.

Maybe a lot of Libertarians don't realize that they too have an inner fire that could make them crusade harder. Our home country is not on the brink of collapse through ozone depletion and neither through immigration. The state as source of all woes cannot be trusted to save us from the real or imagined problems. Actually it's the Orwellian threat of a totalitarian state, of total surveillance and final destruction of private property, which has for a long time been in the works from Merkel to Maas and is about to be completed. This threat is real, concrete - and humongous. A bad feeling, even naked dread, is already wide-spread. Libertarians have only to pick up this thread - and to make it clear that this danger cannot be banned through "different politics", but it is the eventual result of politization of all parts of life, a statist vicious circle of interventionism, which as "the death wish of history" (Igor R. Schafarewitsch) once again strives towards its natural, institutional goal. If this time millions of casualties can be prevented, then trying to should be worth some effort. For home, for lawfulness and for our own lives.
